fills.researcher_notes: ONE QUESTION PER COMPANY, answered once for the whole Central Asia-Center system and applied across all 4 rows in this brief (P2291/P2292/P5770/P5771), per the brief's instruction. Established: AO Intergas Central Asia -- a subsidiary of AO KazTransGas/QazaqGaz -- operates the KAZAKH section of the Central Asia-Center system (the brief's transit-corridor guidance: name the entity operating the Kazakh section specifically, not Gazprom/Turkmengaz/Uztransgaz who hold the non-Kazakh sections). Two genuinely independent origins plus one supporting wire report: (1) Intergas Central Asia's own official corporate page (intergas.kz/ru/obwaya-informaciya/) lists the trunk systems its regional Управления магистральных газопроводов (UMG branches -- Atyrau, Aktau, Uralsk) maintain, including verbatim 'МГ «Средняя Азия - Центр» с лупингами'; (2) AO KazTransGas's 50th-anniversary press release on the pipeline (syndicated at nangs.org, same corporate family as (1) so counted as one origin with it) states verbatim 'АО «Интергаз Центральная Азия», входящая в состав АО «КазТрансГаз»' operates the Kazakh section via 7 branch management offices; (3) a GENUINELY THIRD-PARTY, non-Kazakhstani source -- Shamil Yenikeyeff, 'Kazakhstan's Gas: Export Markets and Export Routes' (Oxford Institute for Energy Studies, working paper NG25, 2008), p.32: 'Under the current arrangements with the Kazakh government, Intergaz Central Asia manages the gas trunk pipelines in the Republic and is responsible for transportation, storage and sales of natural gas... Intergaz Central Asia controls the following gas pipelines: - Central Asia-Centre pipeline (for gas volumes from Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan)...' -- confirms the same fact from outside Kazakhstan's own corporate/press ecosystem, so (1)/(2) and (3) count as 2 independent origins overall -> tier=high. Also consistent with an August 2025 Interfax wire (interfax.com/newsroom/top-stories/113443, genuinely independent news source) reporting QazaqGaz completing repair work on a stretch of the CAC pipeline. url_verifier.py: intergas.kz and nangs.org both OK (200, expected substring present). Never cited gem.wiki, which names the same 4 operators (Turkmengaz/Intergas Central Asia/Gazprom/Uztransgaz) without specifying which one operates the Kazakh section -- this research narrows that down and sources it independently. validity.researcher_notes: ENDPOINT_COUNTRY: the route's first vertex (45.314, 55.250) sits ~0.3-4km from Beyneu, Mangystau (real-world Beyneu ≈ 45.317N, 55.200E) -- i.e. it matches this row's OWN StartLocation field ('Beyneu') almost exactly. This is not a drawing error: en.wikipedia /ru.wikipedia (Газопровод Центральная Азия - Центр) both describe CAC-3 (the western branch) as running 'from Okarem, near the Turkmenistan-Iran border, ... through Zhanaozen in Kazakhstan to Beyneu compressor station, where it meets the eastern branch' -- i.e. Beyneu is a real waypoint/junction on this line, not its true international origin. So the drawn geometry covers only the Beyneu(Kazakhstan)->Gubkin(Russia) leg of a pipeline whose StartCountryOrArea='Turkmenistan'/EndCountryOrArea='Russia' describe the pipeline's overall transnational endpoints (true gas origin at Okarem, ultimate Russian destination), not the drawn segment's own endpoints. Verdict: correctly-drawn partial route, not a data defect -- do not propose new coordinates, per protocol.

validity.researcher_notes: LENGTH_RATIO: same read as the endpoint flag above, and the two are not independent questions -- both follow from the route being a PARTIAL draw (Beyneu->Gubkin only, 1569km measured) of a string whose StartCountryOrArea/EndCountryOrArea describe the full Turkmenistan-to-Russia transit. 2600km is too small to be the 5-string CAC system aggregate (KMG AR2019/2020: 5,306km; AR2021: 4,149.2km, across all of CAC-1..5) and too large to be the drawn Beyneu-Gubkin leg alone (1569km) -- it sits in between, which is consistent with being CAC-3's OWN full transnational length (Okarem, Turkmenistan -> Beyneu, Kazakhstan -> Gubkin, Russia). Supporting arithmetic, not proof: Yenikeyeff/OIES 2008 Table 10 (p.33) gives CAC-3's KAZAKHSTAN-portion length (the pre-Beyneu stretch, built 1974) as 754km, a stretch the drawn route does NOT cover (the route starts AT Beyneu); 2600 - 1569(drawn) = 1031km unaccounted-for, the right order of magnitude for a Turkmenistan+pre-Beyneu-Kazakhstan stretch of ~754km-plus-Turkmen-mileage. This is a reasoned inference from segment-level data (tier=low; I could not find a source stating 2600km for CAC-3 directly), not a confirmed match -- UNRESOLVED on the exact figure, but the 'own full-transnational-length on a Kazakh-portion route' explanation should replace the 'system aggregate copied onto a string' hypothesis in the brief.
